title: Runtime contracts and CI validators for load-harness reproducibility
creator: Asha Patel
description: Standardize a strict runtime contract (driver/CUDA/container digest/runner config) and add CI-time validators so our tokens/sec and p95 load-harness results are reproducible across CI, local engineer runs, and dedicated fleets. This ticket covers the contract definition, CI validator implementation, baseline capture, and dashboarding integration for regression detection.
acceptance_criteria: A formal runtime contract document exists and is linked from the benchmark repo (defines supported driver versions, CUDA versions, base OS images, and how container images must be pinned to digest).
CI validator added to the benchmark repo that fails PRs if a benchmark configuration references unpinned images or unsupported driver/CUDA pairings.

Baseline artifacts (tokens/sec and p95) are captured for the canonical matrix and stored in s3://redwood-benchmarks/baselines/runtime-1.20/ with CI jobs that can update baselines behind a gated workflow.
Regression detection rule configured: p95 latency increase > 10% or tokens/sec decrease > 12% compared to baseline triggers a blocking CI status with details and links to failure traces.
Dashboard shows per-run tokens/sec and p95 with a comparison line to baseline and flagging for outliers; dashboard tile added to Runtime Stability board.
Documentation for engineers (how to run the harness locally, how to add new driver/CUDA combos) is published to Confluence and linked from the README.
tasks: Draft runtime contract (include precise driver package names and minimum/maximum supported CUDA versions).
Add image-pin linter to benchmark config parsing (reject tags, require @sha256 digests).
Implement CI validator job in .github/workflows/benchmark-validate.yml that reads runtime contract and lints configs.
Create baseline capture job that runs canonical load matrix nightly and uploads artifacts to S3 with metadata (git sha, image digest, runner id).
Integrate regression detector into PR status: compute delta vs baseline and annotate PR with metrics and links to traces.
Update k8s runner node-label mapping and provision small pool for deterministic kernels used by the harness.
Add dashboard panel and create alert rule for sustained regression across 3 consecutive runs.
Write engineer-facing runbook for adding/changing driver or CUDA rows to matrix including hardware probe steps.
notes: 2026-03-02: Kickoff sync — aligned on one canonical matrix (x86 A100 80GB, x86 8xA10G, arm 4xH100) for initial rollout; agreed to start with driver 535 and CUDA 12.1 as the reference point.

2026-03-04: Decided to require image digest pinning (@sha256) for all runtime images used in benchmark configs to eliminate tag drift. Trade-off: slightly more friction for authors; benefit: full reproducibility.
2026-03-06: Design review feedback from Lin Zhao — suggested storing runner hardware telemetry (GPU clock state, MIG config) alongside baseline to aid triage. Added to tasks.
2026-03-08: PR #781 in github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-runner adds image linter and first CI validator (see links). Waiting on code owner review from infra-team.

2026-03-10: Mateo ran the smoke matrix locally against pinned images; tokens/sec variance within +/-6% for canonical runs, p95 within +/-8% — close to acceptance but need automated baseline capture and CI gating.
review_feedback: Lin Zhao: please include GPU power/clock headroom in baseline metadata — it explains ~5-7% variance in tokens/sec.
Priya Menon (QA): CI validator should allow an explicit 'experimental' tag for new driver/CUDA combos that are gated behind an opt-in flag.
Danielle Park (Security): confirm that pinned image digests are scanned with the SCA pipeline and that the CI job surfaces SCA results.
planned_rollout: Phase 1 (Week 1): Land contract docs and image linter in benchmark-runner repo; add CI validator that warns (non-blocking) to get initial adoption.
Phase 2 (Week 2): Enable blocking mode for unpinned images and unsupported driver/CUDA combos; run full nightly baseline capture.
Phase 3 (Week 3): Hook regression detector into PR checks and dashboard alerts; run canary on dedicated fleet for one week before defaulting to all runs.
